about: Call-category taxonomy for Answering AI leads. A firm's contact-type names (free text, ~4,400 distinct) map to one category, an optional practice area, and modifiers. Patterns are Python regexes matched against the name lowercased with punctuation replaced by spaces. Categories are tried in order; the first match wins. See README.md.
systemPrefixAbout: Names starting with '-' are platform entries (admin, numbers, on-call schedules). One that matches no category and no other rule is a system entry; '-Insurance BH' still maps to insurance.

categories.label: System entry
categories.description: Platform bookkeeping, not a kind of call: admin, no-charge, screen pop-up, test entries, phone-number and recording entries, and screening notes about calls the firm does not take ('NOT IN NYC, WC, MASS').

categories.label: New matter
categories.description: A prospective client with a new legal matter: the lead a CRM integration exists for. Checked right after system entries, so 'New Divorce/Custody Call' or 'New Property Insurance' is a new matter, not a custody or insurance call. A name that only names a practice area ('Personal Injury') is also a new matter, but only once no other category matched. The fallback never uses the practice area 'other': 'Other Calls' is General.

categories.label: Existing client
categories.description: A current client calling about their matter. A message for the firm, not a new lead.

categories.label: Jail / custody
categories.description: A call from or about someone in custody, with no new matter named. Often a new criminal matter; firms decide whether it goes to their CRM. 'New Criminal Case (Jail)' is a new matter with the in-custody modifier instead.

categories.label: Court, attorney or agency
categories.description: Courts, judges, clerks, other attorneys, opposing counsel, prosecutors, government agencies and law enforcement.

categories.label: Insurance or medical provider
categories.description: Insurance companies and adjusters, medical providers, no-fault and records requests.

categories.label: Emergency
categories.description: Urgent calls the firm wants escalated immediately.

categories.label: Vendor or solicitation
categories.description: Sales calls, vendors, solicitors. 'Sales / marketing' is the legacy system's own template name for these (RFC-010 §2.1), not a person.

categories.label: General
categories.description: Catch-all: general calls, all calls, messages, returning a call. Firms whose only entry is this one send everything.
categories.pattern: \b(general|all calls?|all spanish|messages?|returning a call|call ?backs?|other calls?|voicemail|calls to voicemail|main line|front desk|google|ads|referrals?|appointments?|scheduling|returning|tech support|human resources|hr|vip|do not call|banks?|family members?|employment inquir\w*|employee inquir\w*|employment calls?|verif(y|ication)\w*|jobs?|applicants?|resumes?)\b

categories.label: Line handling
categories.description: How calls are handled (patch to the firm, take a message, away, after hours, schedule) with no kind of call named. Language and web chat alone are not line handling: 'Spanish Calls' is General with the spanish modifier.

categories.label: Named person
categories.description: Only a person's name: calls for a specific staff member. Says who, not what kind of call. Needs a human to map.
